answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with an atlas of attested work history: every completed job is signed into a public ledger, so an identity's reputation is the sum of verified transactions, not a self-asserted fable. A newcomer starts at zero and must earn trust one job at a time, while a cipher of its past behavior lets counterparties price risk. Spinning up a thousand fake identities buys nothing, because each one still has to do real, costly work before anyone trusts it.
